scope: Native private PMIC BCL wake-failure recovery, managed parent regmap dependency, supplier release/rebind and controlled in-flight IRQ removal; not physical PMIC acceptance
implemented: Track successful native disable_irq_wake before clearing ownership; on threshold disable error preserve armed state and return real error
Do not clear trigger statistics until rearm wake acquisition succeeds
Freeze captures all original actions and restores them on a tested partial wake-drop failure
Restore only acquires missing wake references, records references acquired by that attempt, and unwinds only those; failed unwind retains ownership for a later retry
Quiesce logs a failed wake release and retains its ownership flag for another cleanup attempt instead of falsely claiming native wake_depth zero
Create native managed DL_FLAG_AUTOREMOVE_CONSUMER link to regmap-owning parent before using its resources; the driver core drains BCL before supplier driver remove
After a sleeping status read, an IRQ thread rechecks stopping before further processing
verified: Six new fault cases inspect actual private native IRQ descriptor wake_depth as well as driver flags and recorded chip balances
Disable/drop error leaves native depth1 and armed IRQ; retry releases depth to0 without unbalanced disable
Freeze partial failure restores all original actions; restore rollback failure retains depth1 and retry does not increase it to2
One transient cleanup failure can be retried while the mapping owner remains alive; statistics and bus-restore errors retain retry state
Supplier driver release/rebind repeats three times; consumer reattach uses normal native attach where required after intentional unbind

Hold the actual native IRQ thread inside a RAM status read; concurrent supplier release reaches BCL stopping but cannot destroy regmap/NVMEM until IRQ gate is released; no later RAM reads start after the stop marker
Previous OF/NVMEM/probe, name-limit, ordered voltage-trip and calibration/DT scalar checks remain covered
baseline_failure: Without the explicit regmap supplier link, native supplier release leaves BCL bound and destroys a regmap with an active IRQ-held mutex. The before-link guest was rejected for failed assertions and a mutex_destroy WARN; the final fresh guest passes strict checks
pending: Permanent wake-disable failure during final unbind cannot be reported back through the void driver remove callback; flags/logs are truthful while context exists, but guaranteed final wake release after context destruction/hardware failure is not implemented
Exhaustive concurrent probe/remove/PM/sysfs/hotplug behavior and actual parent driver/IRQ controller variants
Full Stage91 modified HAL/service, every indirect reference and remaining ROM consumers, paired DT/HAL and DT-schema acceptance
